items.title: Henry "Booker T." Glass Interview, 1962-03-22
items.q: You know when I was a kid, after I'd seen the Zulu and then see Rex... I'd see Rex, that's when I had my Carnival.

ctx.x: I'm not going to be there.

He came out there, he ain't going to be there. No, I'm not going to be playing for him. Oh. That's what I said. I'm not going to play for him. Not Carnival, huh? No, not Carnival. I'll be right around here at Carnival. I don't be playing a little short parade like the Zulu. Or maybe if I could land at the Arabian Packing Company, they'd be through at one o'clock in the day. What do you think about the Zulu parade? Do you like it or not? Yeah, I like it. I think it's been going on many years. You know when I was a…

Million dollar dolls. That's right. Them women would be masking, and all of them have a hundred dollar bills. Their whole leg around they're stopping. They may not put no hundred dollar bills in their legs now. Cut their legs off. Cut their legs off. I'd go and hear the music. He loves music. He can play a drum, yeah.
